cards.title: Qualifying Liver-Blood-Flow-Based Clearance Scaling
cards.claim: Liver-blood-flow-based scaling is a candidate extrapolation method when a reference species has compatible clearance and physiological-flow data. The cited multi-compound study found the method useful with primate data, but performance depended on compound class and reference species. This empirical result is not proof that flow limits the target compound clearance.
conditions: Reference-species clearance and body weight are available with unambiguous units.
Reference and target liver blood flow are qualified for the population and expressed on the same absolute or per-body-weight basis.
required_inputs: Reference-species clearance, body weight and parameter basis.
Reference and target liver blood flow with units and provenance.
Target body weight if converting per-body-weight flow to absolute flow; explicit scaling equation.
limitations: The reference study does not establish a universally best species or flow constant.
Nonhepatic clearance, binding and nonlinear processes may invalidate the bridge.
cards.downstream_use: Use as an explicitly qualified comparison scenario, keeping dimensional consistency and method uncertainty.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
